 M. Salah Trabzonspor Trabzonspor vs Freiburg Freiburg Conference League Egypt Türkiye Germany Bottom-table position after the defeat
 Trabzonspor fell to defeat at home against German visitors Freiburg in the third round of the league phase in the UEFA Europa Conference League at the Papara Park stadium.
 Freiburg struck early. Lukas Kübler bundled home a follow-up inside the box in the 14th minute after Onana had failed to deal convincingly with the initial effort.
 Trabzonspor pushed for a way back throughout. Their most dangerous moment fell to Egypt's Mohamed Salah, who chested down a cross and fired over the bar. He also curled a free kick into the wall, threading clever touches into the game with his movement and passing.
 The hosts screamed for a penalty when Nigerian striker Onuachu was shoved in the box, but the referee waved play on.

 After the break, Trabzonspor pumped high balls towards Onuachu and their advancing defenders in search of an equaliser. Nothing came of it. Freiburg, meanwhile, looked dangerous on the counter and from set pieces, coming close to a second more than once.
 Then came Trabzonspor's clearest chance of all. Salah squandered a certain goal from the goal line in the 60th minute, the ball arriving at a corner with the Egyptian stood right in front of the net. Inexplicably, he placed it straight into the hands of the German goalkeeper. The stands erupted in anguish as the equaliser slipped away.
 Defeat did little damage to their standing. Trabzonspor clung on to a direct qualification spot for the round of 16, sitting eighth with 6 points from 3 matches, behind Monaco on goal difference at the top of the mini-table and level with Freiburg, who also moved to 6 points.
 Elsewhere, Atalanta were held to a 1-1 draw by visitors Kairat Almaty of Kazakhstan. Marc Jaull put the Kazakhs ahead in the 53rd minute before Nikola Krstovic rescued a point for Atalanta with a late strike (82).
 Red Star Belgrade turned it around against visitors Inter d'Escaldes to seal a late 2-1 win in a match that produced two red cards, one for each side.
 Arellano had handed the visitors the lead before Vladimir Lucic levelled for Red Star. Yuta Nakayama then snatched the killer winner in stoppage time.
 In the same round, Ajax ran riot at Midtjylland of Denmark, winning 6-1. Nigerian Tolulope Arokodare opened the scoring early and grabbed a second for himself, with Owen Wijndal, Davy Klaassen, Oscar Gloukh and Marcus Leonardo piling on the misery. Friday Etim bagged Midtjylland's only consolation.
